questions.question:

**The correct answer is option 4.**

No other option is suitable.

So, 'anything since' is correct.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

'An' is used before words that begin with vowel sounds (a,e,i,o,u). We check the sounds. 'European' begins with 'e' but starts with the sound 'y' which is not a vowel. So, we will use 'a European'.

'The' is used before definite nouns.

So, option 1 is correct.

questions.question:
The statements below are followed by two conclusions labelled I and II. Assuming that the information in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with generally established facts, decide which conclusion(s) logically and definitely follow(s) from the information given in the statements.

**Statements:**

I. Some cups are glasses.

II. No plate is cup as well as glass.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some cups are plates.

II. All glasses are not plates.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor conclusion II follow
Either conclusion I or conclusion II follows.

questions.solution:
Possible van diagram from the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0e4f1fd912559a76c19a7f6d107ae02ce53c168acca8f4bc9e254cf835b65a3c.png] 

I. Some cups are plates → **False **(The statements do not provide any information confirming that cups and plates must overlap. While it's possible, it is not a definite logical necessity)

II. All glasses are not plates → **False **(This is a universal negative statement. The second statement only says a plate cannot be both at once. It does not forbid a plate from being a glass (provided that glass isn't also a cup). Therefore, we cannot say with certainty that no glasses are plates.)

Since none of the conclusion is true.

**Hence, the correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: The cost of an article is Rs. 480. It is to be sold at a profit of 12.5%. What is the selling price of the article?
questions.solution:
Given C.P = Rs. 480

Profit % = 12.5%

Since, S.P = C.P × (1 + profit%/100)

So, S.P = 480 × (1 + 12.5/100)

⇒ S.P = 480 × 9/8

∴ The selling price of the article is Rs. 540

questions.question: If 4A = 6B = 5C; then find the value of A : B : C.
questions.solution:
Let 4A = 6B = 5C = K

⇒ 4A = K, 6B = K and 5C = K

⇒ A = K/4, B = K/6 and C = K/5

Now, A : B : C = K/4 : K/6 : K/5

Since, LCM of 4, 6 and 5 = 60

⇒ Multiply (60/K) in each term of the above ratio

⇒ A : B : C = (K/4 × 60/k) : (K/6 × 60/k) : (K/5 × 60/k)

∴ A : B : C = 15 : 10 : 12

questions.question: Which human organ is responsible for removing nitrogenous waste from the human body?

• Here **kidney __plays an important role in the purification of blood by removing the wastes. It removes the urea which is excreted out and blood goes back to the heart again. **
 
• Excess water is flushed out in the form of urine but the kidney helps the body to retain the necessary amount of water.

lungs are sponge-like organs.

 
 
 
 Every time person breathe lungs filter oxygen from the air.

 
 
 
lungs filter carbon dioxide from your body when you breathe out.

kidneys are also filters.

questions.question: The decisions of the Supreme Court of India are binding on _________.

options.text: All States & UT except J & K

questions.solution:
__
 
• In India, the Supreme court is at the helm of judicial structure in India.
 
• The Supreme Court and High Courts are also called the court of record. It means that they the power to punish anyone for contempt of its orders.
 
• **Again, Article 141 of the constitution of India provides that the orders of the Supreme Court shall be binding on the other courts within the territory of India.**
 
• It is pertinent to note here that although the Supreme Court's decision is binding on all courts of India, it is **not binding on Supreme Court itself**__ which means that __**Supreme Court do has the power to override it's earlier decisions**__.
 
• However, the general superintendence of the district and other subordinate courts in any state is vested in their respective high courts.
 
• But the orders passed by the Supreme Court can supersede that of any High Court. Supreme Court is also a __**highest court of appeal**__ in India.

questions.question: Which is the highest Court of Appeal in India?
questions.solution:
__
 
• In India there is a system of the single-integrated judiciary, meaning there is only one court for both laws enacted by Union (Parliament) and States (their Legislative Assemblies).
 
• However, there is a hierarchical structure of courts with the supreme court at the helm followed by high courts and then the subordinate courts.
 
• Article 124 of the Constitution of India mandates having a **Supreme court**__.
 
• Historically the supreme court was created by the Government of India act 1935 as Federal Court but after the enactment of the constitution, it was revamped as the present-day supreme court.
 
• Supreme court in its capacity acts as the prime resolver of Federal disputes between central or state or between two or more states.
 
• It is the guardian of Fundamental Rights and interpreter of the constitution.
 
• **It also acts as the highest court of appeal in India. **

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a colour in the Olympic Ring?
questions.solution:
__
 
• For the first time, the Olympic Rings were presented in 1913.
 
• The design of these rings was created by Pierre de Coubertin.
 
• This symbol** consists of five rings of equal size** and **represents five continents of the world **__as this sporting event is a meeting of athletes from all these continents.
 
• These five rings are represented either in one colour or five different colours. When depicted in five colours it includes (from left to right): 
 
 
• **Blue, Black, Red on the top.**
 
• **Yellow and Green at the bottom.**
 
 
 
• **There is no pink colour.**

questions.question: Which part of human respiratory system provides surface for exchange of gases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Alveoli**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The main function of the human respiratory system is to Inhale the air and using the Oxygen present in the air then transported to different body parts and using that oxygen food is broken down to be stored in form of energy (ATP).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 
 
__**Organ**__

 
 
 
__**Function**__

 
 
 

 
 
Nostril

 
 
 
Air is taken in via nostrils and passes through the nasal cavity.

 
 
 

 
 
Trachea

 
 
 
It is a long tube passing through the mid-thoracic cavity.

 
 
 

 
 
Bronchi

 
 
 
The trachea is later divided into two bronchi. The trachea and bronchi moisten the air flowing through with the help of ciliated epithelial cells and goblet cells (secretory cells)

 
 
 

 
 
Bronchioles

 
 
 
Each bronchus is further divided into finer channels known as bronchioles

 
 
 

 
 
__**Alveoli**__

 
 
 
And bronchioles into balloon-like structures called alveoli. Air reaches alveoli via bronchus and bronchioles.** It is the alveoli which provide the surface for human respiration. **

questions.question: The famous Lingraja Temple is located in which city?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The famous Lingaraj temple was built** **by king Jajati Keshari of Soma Vansh during the 11th century.
 
• **This temple is located in the city of Bhubaneshwar__. **
 
• This temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva.
 
• The Linga of Lord Shiva is worshipped which is considered to be swaymbhu (self-originating).
 
• Also, one of the characteristic worships of this temple includes combined worship of Shiva and Vishnu in "Hari-Hara" form together.
 
• Another famous temple of** Lord Shiva is located in Ujjain and is known as Mahakaleswara temple**.

questions.question: Which of the following pillars depict rock-cut pillars?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Maurya Pillar**__ Architecture was comprised of four parts: 

 
 
• Shaft: a long shaft from the ground which provided a base and was usually made of a single stone or cut out of a single monolith.
 
• Capital: upon that shaft was capital usually lotus or something bell-shaped.
 
• Abacus: provided resting platform for the figure which was put on top.
 
• Capital Figure: usually a Lion, Elephant, or bull either standing or sitting was carved on the top.
 
 
 
• Both Mauryan and Achemeninan (Persian) pillars used polished stones.
 
• **Mauryan Pillars** were rock-cut out of single monoliths.
 
• **Gothic pillar **comes within Gothic Architecture which is also called Pointed Architecture.
 
 
• Three essential elements of Gothic Architecture are:
 
 
• I) The pointed arch
 
• II) The rib vault
 
• III) The flying buttress
 
 
 
 
 
• **Achaemenid Architecture **(**Persian**) is an extraordinary architectural legacy starting from Cyrus the Great's solemn tomb in Pasargadae to the extraordinary structures of the Persepolis.
